10.0.old: The reserve is the next seat unless it is JFL-moved or time-removed, in which case there is no reserve.
10.0.new: The reserve is the first seat after the panel that is neither JFL-moved nor time-removed; if none is, there is no reserve (ASK 629; Init Seats). A reserve that substituted is not offered again as an alternate, because G3 refuses a model already on the panel; a reserve that was not used is still offered. Not shown by a run.

10.0.new:
Panel Check classifies each slot (error, timeout, refused, no usable judgment). A reply whose message content is not text is no usable judgment, and its detail names the cause: `returned no text: finish_reason ; output tokens (reasoning ); prompt tokens

` (ASK 629; a field the provider did not give prints "not given"); with no reserve free the run fails closed with `FAIL-CLOSED: seat "" returned no text: ... NO ROW IS WRITTEN.` and "[no reserve seat is free]".

16.0.old: 2. A panel seat fails closed with "an envelope this parser does not recognise" -> often `finish_reason: length` with empty content: the reasoning used the whole limit -> read the seat's `failed_reply` in `debate_enforcer_log`; the parser's message misnames the cause.
16.0.new: 2. A panel seat fails with "returned no text: finish_reason length; output tokens <n> (reasoning <r>)" -> the reasoning used the whole limit -> read the reply: in `ppj_replies` for a run that failed closed (such a run stores no enforcer rows), or in the seat's `failed_reply` row of `debate_enforcer_log` where a reserve substituted; the limit is the seat's `model_config.max_tokens`, and no reasoning setting is changed without the operator's instruction (§4). "An envelope this parser does not recognise" names any other reply form the parser cannot read.
